title: Turbocharger Overboost Condition
shortDescription: Boost pressure exceeds the commanded ceiling.
fullDescription:
P0234 sets when the ECM detects boost pressure exceeding the maximum allowable threshold versus the commanded value. The control strategy aborts further boost and may force limp mode.

Causes range from a stuck wastegate to a failed boost-control solenoid or a misreporting MAP sensor. Mechanical damage to internals can occur if ignored.
safetyImpact: Possible engine damage if boost runs unchecked; reduce throttle and address promptly.

fixSteps.title: Read freeze-frame data
fixSteps.instruction: Capture boost commanded vs actual at fault.

fixSteps.title: Test boost solenoid and wastegate
fixSteps.instruction: Bench-test solenoid resistance and verify wastegate moves freely.

fixSteps.title: Replace faulty component
fixSteps.instruction: Solenoid, sensor, or actuator as indicated.

faq.a: Limp-mode is likely; repair before forcing engine to compensate.
Yes - prolonged uncontrolled boost or constant overrun stresses bearings.

title: Turbocharger Boost Sensor A Circuit
shortDescription: Boost-pressure sensor A circuit malfunction.
fullDescription:
P0235 indicates a general fault on the boost-pressure sensor A circuit - signal out of range or implausible compared to other inputs.

Most commonly the sensor itself or its wiring is at fault, but ECM faults can occur. Boost trims default to safe values.
safetyImpact: Reduced power; safe to drive briefly to a shop.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check for chafe at turbo heat shield.

faq.a: Yes, but in a derate.
Clear DTCs and verify under load.

title: Turbocharger Boost Sensor A Range/Performance
shortDescription: Boost sensor A reading is implausible vs other inputs.
fullDescription:
P0236 sets when sensor A reports values that don't agree with MAF, BARO, or commanded duty during stable conditions.

A contaminated MAP/boost sensor or kinked reference line is typical. Boost control may be conservative until cleared.
safetyImpact: Power may be reduced; not immediately unsafe.

faq.a: Oil residue from PCV path.
Mild surge possible.

title: Turbocharger Boost Sensor A Circuit Low
shortDescription: Boost sensor A signal voltage below expected minimum.
fullDescription:
P0237 means the boost-sensor signal is sitting at or below its low limit, suggesting an open, short to ground, or failed sensor.

The ECM treats output as default and limits boost. Repair the wiring or sensor to restore performance.
safetyImpact: Limp mode likely.

faq.a: ECM substitutes a safe value.
Yes, then verify with PID log.

title: Turbocharger Boost Sensor A Circuit High
shortDescription: Boost-pressure sensor signal above expected maximum.
fullDescription:
P0238 sets when the boost-sensor signal is stuck at the upper rail, indicating a short to voltage or open ground.

The ECM disables turbo control to protect the engine. Ground integrity and 5V reference are the first checks.
safetyImpact: Limp mode and reduced power; not directly unsafe.

faq.a: Rare - check wiring first.
Only after repair and drive cycle.

title: Turbocharger Underboost Condition
shortDescription: Boost pressure consistently below commanded.
fullDescription:
P0299 indicates the commanded boost is not being achieved - typical causes are charge-air leaks, a stuck-open wastegate, or a worn turbo.

This is one of the most common turbo codes and often shows up alongside boost-leak symptoms like a hissing intake.
safetyImpact: Reduced acceleration; not unsafe but address before towing.

fixSteps.instruction: Bench-test solenoid resistance and verify wastegate moves freely.

fixSteps.instruction: Solenoid, sensor, or actuator as indicated.

faq.a: Replacing a split charge-pipe coupler.
On diesels yes - check exhaust restriction.

title: Cyl 1 Glow Plug Module Comm Lost
shortDescription: Loss of glow-plug module communication for cylinder 1.
fullDescription:
P02CB indicates a serial-bus or supply-side fault between the ECM and the glow-plug control module on the listed cylinder. This blocks cold-start preheat for that cylinder.

Diagnosis focuses on module power, ground, and CAN/LIN traffic. A failed glow-plug module is the most common cause.
safetyImpact: Hard cold start expected; engine still runs once warm.

faq.a: Yes - this code only applies to compression-ignition engines.
It will start hard - address before winter.

title: Cyl 9 Glow Plug Module Comm Lost
shortDescription: Loss of glow-plug module communication for cylinder 9.
fullDescription:
P02D3 sets when the ECM cannot reach the cylinder-9 glow-plug controller. Mostly seen on V8 / V10 diesels.

Check wiring loom routing across the rocker cover area where heat damage is common.
safetyImpact: Cold start handicapped; warm engine unaffected.

faq.a: Yes once warm.
Less symptom but still active.

title: Cyl 10 Glow Plug Module Comm Lost
shortDescription: Loss of glow-plug module communication for cylinder 10.
fullDescription:
P02D4 occurs when communications with the cylinder-10 glow-plug driver fail. Wiring and module faults dominate.

Verify CAN/LIN integrity to the module and inspect connector for moisture.
safetyImpact: Hard cold start; otherwise drivable.

faq.a: Often yes on modern diesels.

title: Cyl 11 Glow Plug Module Comm Lost
shortDescription: Loss of glow-plug module communication for cylinder 11.
fullDescription:
P02D5 covers cylinder-11 glow-plug driver communication loss. Found on heavy-duty V12 diesels.

Diagnosis matches other PXXX glow-plug codes - module power, ground, and bus integrity.
safetyImpact: Cold-start handicap.

faq.a: Mostly.

title: Turbo/Super Boost Control A Circuit/Open
shortDescription: Turbocharger control circuit fault: open.
fullDescription:
P0045 indicates a fault in the turbo/supercharger boost-control actuator circuit (open). The ECM cannot achieve commanded boost and forces a default mode.

Look at solenoid wiring, actuator integrity, and overlapping codes for boost sensor or wastegate position.
safetyImpact: Reduced power; turbine overspeed can damage the turbo.

A fault can produce both over- and under-boost conditions and surge during gear changes.

title: Intercooler Bypass Valve Position Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: Intercooler bypass valve position sensor: circuit malfunction.
fullDescription:
P02D6 sets when the intercooler bypass valve position feedback is faulty (circuit malfunction). With imprecise feedback, the ECM cannot manage the bypass during light-load operation.

Fuel economy and cold-start emissions can suffer until corrected.
safetyImpact: Mild driveability/economy loss only.

title: Intake Air Diverter Valve Control Circuit
shortDescription: Intake air diverter valve: control circuit malfunction.
fullDescription:
P02E1 indicates the intake air diverter (recirculation) valve is reporting control circuit malfunction. The ECM uses this valve to manage compressor pressure during throttle release.

Left uncorrected, the result is compressor surge or persistent over/underboost during shifts.
safetyImpact: Surge can damage turbo bearings over time.
